title: Bekhorot 47
description: Does a convert who already had children as a gentile have a firstborn heir? Then whose son is exempt from the five sela: the Levite’s daughter, the priest’s daughter and the ḥalal son of a priest who died; the son of uncertain paternity and the brother born after him; and the miscarriages and caesarean births that decide who counts as a firstborn.

a2.he: אִיתְּמַר: הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים בְּגַיּוּתוֹ וְנִתְגַּיֵּיר — רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אוֹמֵר: אֵין לוֹ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ לוֹ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה. רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אוֹמֵר: אֵין לוֹ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה — דְּהָא הֲוָה לֵיהּ ״רֵאשִׁית אוֹנוֹ״, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אוֹמֵר: יֵשׁ לוֹ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה — גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד דָּמֵי.

a3.he: וְאָזְדוּ לְטַעְמַיְיהוּ, דְּאִיתְּמַר: הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים בְּגַיּוּתוֹ וְנִתְגַּיֵּיר — רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: קִיֵּים פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לֹא קִיֵּים. רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: קִיֵּים — ״לֹא תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ״, וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: לֹא קִיֵּים פְּרִיָּה וּרְבִיָּה — גֵּר שֶׁנִּתְגַּיֵּיר כְּקָטָן שֶׁנּוֹלַד דָּמֵי.

a4.he: וּצְרִיכָא, דְּאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָא קַמַּיְיתָא, בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, מִשּׁוּם דִּבְגַיּוּתָן לָאו בְּנֵי נַחֲלָה נִינְהוּ, אֲבָל בְּהָא אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, דְּ״לֹא תֹהוּ בְּרָאָהּ לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ״, וְהָא עֲבַד לֵיהּ שֶׁבֶת.

a5.he: וְאִי אִיתְּמַר בְּהָא, בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, אֲבָל בְּהָא אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, צְרִיכָא.

a6.he: תְּנַן: מִי שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים, וְנָשָׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁכְּבָר יָלְדָה, עוֹדָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְנִשְׁתַּחְרְרָה, עוֹדָהּ גּוֹיָה וְנִתְגַּיְּירָה, וּמִשֶּׁבָּאתָה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל יָלָדָה — וְלָדָהּ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְאֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן.

a7.he: יָלְדָה מִמַּאן? אִילֵימָא מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים — מַאי אִירְיָא גִּיּוֹרֶת וְשִׁפְחָה? אֲפִילּוּ בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי!

a8.he: אֶלָּא לָאו מִגֵּר שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים וְנִתְגַּיֵּיר, וְקָתָנֵי בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה!

a9.he: לָא, לְעוֹלָם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים, וְ״אֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן״ אִיצְטְרִיכָא לֵיהּ.

a10.he: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, דְּאָמַר: בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְלַכֹּהֵן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ — עַד שֶׁיִּפְטְרוּ רֶחֶם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן דְּלָא.

a11.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים בְּגַיּוּתוֹ וְנִתְגַּיֵּיר, יֵשׁ לוֹ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה! אָמַר רָבִינָא, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב אַחָא: הָא וַדַּאי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי הִוא, דְּאָמַר ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל״ — עַד שֶׁיִּפְטְרוּ רֶחֶם מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וְיָלֵיף אִיהוּ מִינַּהּ דִּידַהּ.

a12.he: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה: לְוִיָּיה שֶׁיָּלְדָה — בְּנָהּ פָּטוּר מֵחֲמֵשׁ סְלָעִים. דְּאִיעַבַּר מִמַּאן? אִילֵימָא דְּאִיעַבַּר מִכֹּהֵן וּמִלֵּוִי, מַאי אִירְיָא לְוִיָּיה? אֲפִילּוּ יִשְׂרְאֵלִית נָמֵי!

a13.he: אֶלָּא דְּאִיעַבַּר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, ״לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם״ כְּתִיב!

a14.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: דְּאִיעַבַּר מִגּוֹי. וְלָא תֵּימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מְזַהֲמִין אֶת הַוָּלָד, אֶלָּא אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְזַהֲמִין אֶת הַוָּלָד, לֵוִי פָּסוּל מִיקְּרֵי.

a15.he: מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא: לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיעַבַּר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, וְשָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דְּאָמַר קְרָא ״פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם״ — בְּפֶטֶר רֶחֶם תְּלָא רַחְמָנָא.

a16.he: תְּנַן: מִי שֶׁהָיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים וְנָשָׂא אִשָּׁה שֶׁלֹּא יָלָדָה, נִתְגַּיְּירָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת, נִשְׁתַּחְרְרָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת.

a17.he: וְיָלְדָה הִיא וְכֹהֶנֶת הִיא, וּלְוִיָּה הִיא, וְאִשָּׁה שֶׁכְּבָר יָלָדָה. וְכֵן מִי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁהֲתָה אַחֲרֵי בַּעְלָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים וְנִשֵּׂאת וְיָלָדָה, וְאֵין יָדוּעַ אִם בֶּן תִּשְׁעָה לָרִאשׁוֹן אִם בֶּן שִׁבְעָה לָאַחֲרוֹן — בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן וְאֵינוֹ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה.

a18.he: מִכְּלָל (דִּכְהוּנָּה) [דְּכֹהֶנֶת] וּלְוִיָּה פְּטוּרִין, דְּאִיעַבַּר מִמַּאן? אִילֵימָא דְּאִיעַבַּר מִכֹּהֵן וְלֵוִי — אִי הָכִי מַאי אִירְיָא כֹּהֶנֶת וּלְוִיָּה? אֲפִילּוּ בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל נָמֵי!

a19.he: אֶלָּא דְּאִיעַבַּר מִגּוֹי — כֹּהֶנֶת פְּטוּרָה? וְהָאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בָּדֵיק לַן רַבָּה, כֹּהֶנֶת שֶׁנִּתְעַבְּרָה מִגּוֹי מַהוּ? וְאָמֵינָא לֵיהּ: לָאו הַיְינוּ דְּרַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה, דְּאָמַר: לְוִיָּה שֶׁיָּלְדָה בְּנָהּ פָּטוּר מֵחָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים?

a20.he: וַאֲמַר לִי: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא?! בִּשְׁלָמָא לְוִיָּה בִּקְדוּשְׁתַּהּ קָיְימָא, דְּתַנְיָא: לְוִיָּה שֶׁנִּשְׁבֵּית אוֹ שֶׁנִּבְעֲלָה בְּעִילַת זְנוּת — נוֹתְנִין לָהּ מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר וְאוֹכֶלֶת.

a21.he: אֶלָּא כֹּהֶנֶת, כֵּיוָן דְּאִי בָּעֵיל לַהּ, הָוְיָא זָרָה!

a22.he: הָנִיחָא לְמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרָבָא, דְּאָמַר דְּאִיעַבַּר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, מוֹקֵי לַהּ בִּדְאִיעַבַּר מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל, אֶלָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא בְּמַאי מוֹקֵי לָהּ?

a23.he: לְעוֹלָם דְּאִיעַבַּר מִכֹּהֵן, וְהִיא בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְאַמַּאי קָרֵי לַהּ ״כֹּהֶנֶת״? דִּבְנָה כֹּהֵן.

b1.he: אִיתְּמַר: כֹּהֵן שֶׁמֵּת וְהִנִּיחַ בֵּן חָלָל — רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: הַבֵּן חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ, רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: אֵין חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ. כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּמֵת הָאָב לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּאֵין הַבֵּן חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי זָכָה אָבִיו בְּפִדְיוֹנוֹ.

b2.he: כִּי פְּלִיגִי הֵיכָא דְּמֵת הָאָב בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר: הַבֵּן חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ, דְּהָא לֹא זָכָה אָבִיו (לְפִדְיוֹנוֹ) [בְּפִדְיוֹנוֹ]. רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: אֵין הַבֵּן חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹת עַצְמוֹ, דַּאֲמַר לֵיהּ: אָתֵינָא מִכֹּחַ גַּבְרָא דְּלָא מָצֵית לְאִשְׁתַּעוֹיֵי דִּינָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ.

b3.he: תְּנַן: נִתְגַּיְּירָה מְעוּבֶּרֶת — בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן, וְאַמַּאי? לֵימָא לֵיהּ: אָתֵינָא מִכֹּחַ גַּבְרָא דְּלָא מָצֵית לְאִשְׁתַּעוֹיֵי דִּינָא בַּהֲדֵיהּ! שָׁאנֵי גּוֹי דְּלֵית לֵיהּ חַיִיס.

b4.he: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן יָאסִינְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: כֹּהֵן שֶׁמֵּת בְּתוֹךְ שְׁלֹשִׁים וְהִנִּיחַ בֵּן חָלָל — הַבֵּן חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁלֹּא זָכָה הָאָב בְּפִדְיוֹנוֹ. מֵת לְאַחַר שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם — אֵין הַבֵּן חַיָּיב לִפְדּוֹת עַצְמוֹ, שֶׁהֲרֵי זָכָה הָאָב בְּפִדְיוֹנוֹ.

b5.he: וְכֵן מִי שֶׁלֹּא שָׁהֲתָה אַחֲרֵי בַּעְלָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה חֳדָשִׁים וְכוּ׳.

b6.he: בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה הוּא דְּלָא הָוֵי, הָא כְּפָשׁוּט שָׁקֵיל. וְאַמַּאי? לֵיזִיל לְגַבַּי הַאי וְלִידְחֲיֵיהּ, וּלְגַבַּי הַאי וְלִידְחֲיֵיהּ!

b7.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: לֹא נִצְרְכָא אֶלָּא לַבָּא אַחֲרָיו, וְהָכִי קָאָמַר: בְּכוֹר לַכֹּהֵן, וְהַבָּא אַחֲרָיו אֵין בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה.

b8.he: וְלִכְתְּבוּ הַרְשָׁאָה לַהֲדָדֵי! וְכִי תֵּימָא: מַתְנִיתִין שֶׁלֹּא בְּהַרְשָׁאָה — הָא מוֹקְמִינַן לַהּ קַמַּן דִּבְהַרְשָׁאָה!

b9.he: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יַנַּאי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי: הוּכְּרוּ וּלְבַסּוֹף נִתְעָרְבוּ — כּוֹתְבִין הַרְשָׁאָה זֶה לָזֶה,

b10.he: לֹא הוּכְּרוּ וּבְסוֹף נִתְעָרְבוּ — אֵין כּוֹתְבִין הַרְשָׁאָה זֶה לָזֶה.

b11.he: מַתְנִי׳ אֵי זֶהוּ בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וְלַכֹּהֵן? הַמַּפֶּלֶת שַׁפִּיר מָלֵא מַיִם, מָלֵא דָּם, מְלֵא גְּנִינִין, הַמַּפֶּלֶת כְּמִין דָּגִים וַחֲגָבִים שְׁקָצִים וּרְמָשִׂים, וְהַמַּפֶּלֶת לְיוֹם אַרְבָּעִים — הַבָּא אַחֲרֵיהֶם בְּכוֹר לַנַּחֲלָה וּלְכֹהֵן.

b12.he: יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן, וְהַבָּא אַחֲרָיו — שְׁנֵיהֶן אֵינָן בְּכוֹר, לֹא לַנַּחֲלָה וְלֹא לַכֹּהֵן. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הָרִאשׁוֹן לַנַּחֲלָה, וְהַשֵּׁנִי לְחָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים.

b13.he: גְּמָ׳ רִאשׁוֹן לַנַּחֲלָה לֹא — ״וְיָלְדוּ לוֹ״ בָּעֵינַן, לְחָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים נָמֵי לָא — ״פָּטַר רֶחֶם״ בָּעֵינַן.

b14.he: שֵׁנִי לַנַּחֲלָה לֹא — ״רֵאשִׁית אוֹנוֹ״ בָּעֵינַן, לְחָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים נָמֵי לָא — קָסָבַר: בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד לָא הָוֵי בְּכוֹר.

b15.he: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: הָרִאשׁוֹן לַנַּחֲלָה, וְהַשֵּׁנִי לְחָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים. רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר: ״תֵּלֵד״ לְרַבּוֹת יוֹצֵא דּוֹפֶן.

b16.he: וְהַשֵּׁנִי לְחָמֵשׁ סְלָעִים, קָסָבַר: בְּכוֹר לְדָבָר אֶחָד הָוֵי בְּכוֹר.

messages.text: Continued from 46b. Rabbi Yoḥanan holds that the emergence of the forehead counts as birth even for inheritance. Against him the Gemara cited the rule that witnesses to a husband’s death must see the face with the nose, and began a second answer: “And if you wish, say:”
The requirement of “He shall recognize” with regard to a firstborn for inheritance, and the recognition of a husband’s face, are discrete matters.

notes.he: דלא כתיב פנים הוי פדחת היכר:
notes.en: “He shall recognize” is a separate matter: since “face” is not written there, the forehead counts as recognition.

notes.he: דכיון דלא כתיב ביה [פנים] בהכרת פדחת לחוד סגי לנחלה והכא דבעי פרצוף פנים משום דכתיב ביה הכרת פניהם:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: “He shall recognize” is a separate matter. Since “face” is not written there, recognizing the forehead alone is enough for inheritance. And here [for a husband’s death] the countenance of the face is required, because “the recognition of their countenance” is written there.

messages.text: It was stated that amora’im engaged in a dispute concerning the case of a man who had children when he was a gentile and he subsequently converted:
He does not have a firstborn with regard to inheritance, i.e., a son who is his firstborn after his conversion does not inherit a double portion.
He does have a firstborn with regard to inheritance.

He does not have a firstborn with regard to inheritance, as this man already had “the first of his strength” (Deuteronomy 21:17), the Torah’s description of the firstborn in this context, before he converted.

verse.he: כִּי אֶת־הַבְּכֹר בֶּן־הַשְּׂנוּאָה יַכִּיר לָתֶת לוֹ פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר־יִמָּצֵא לוֹ כִּי־הוּא רֵאשִׁית אֹנוֹ לוֹ מִשְׁפַּט הַבְּכֹרָה׃ {ס}
verse.en: Instead, he must accept the first-born, the son of the unloved one, and allot to him a double portion of all he possesses; since he is the first fruit of his vigor, the birthright is his due.

messages.text: He does have a firstborn with regard to inheritance, as the halakhic status of a convert who just converted is like that of a child just born.

notes.he: עובדי כוכבים אינן בני נחלה לירש את אביהם עובד כוכבים אחר שנתגיירו בפ"ק דקדושין (דף יז:):
notes.en: Gentiles are not heirs: [sons] do not inherit their gentile father once they have converted; [see] the first chapter of Kiddushin (17b).

messages.text: And these amora’im follow their regular line of reasoning, as it was stated: If a man had children when he was a gentile and he subsequently converted,
He has already fulfilled the mitzva to be fruitful and multiply.
He has not fulfilled the mitzva to be fruitful and multiply.

He has fulfilled the aspect of the mitzva to be fruitful and multiply expressed in the command: “He did not create it to be a waste; He formed it to be inhabited” (Isaiah 45:18), i.e., to increase the inhabitation of the world.

verse.he: כִּי כֹה אָמַר־יְהֹוָה בּוֹרֵא הַשָּׁמַיִם הוּא הָאֱלֹהִים יֹצֵר הָאָרֶץ וְעֹשָׂהּ הוּא כוֹנְנָהּ לֹא־תֹהוּ בְרָאָהּ לָשֶׁבֶת יְצָרָהּ אֲנִי יְהֹוָה וְאֵין עוֹד׃
verse.en:
For thus said GOD,
The Creator of heaven who alone is God,
Who formed the earth and made it,
Who alone established it—
Who did not create it a waste,
But formed it for habitation:
I am GOD, and there is none else.

notes.he: הקב"ה את העולם אלא לשבת יצרה:
notes.en: He did not create it to be a waste: the Holy One, blessed be He, did not create the world to be a waste, but formed it to be inhabited.

messages.text: He has not fulfilled the mitzva to be fruitful and multiply, as the halakhic status of a convert who just converted is like that of a child just born, and it is considered as though he did not have children.

And it is necessary to state their opinions in both cases. As, if it were stated only in that first case with regard to inheritance, perhaps it is only in that case that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says his opinion that the first son born after conversion inherits a double portion, because in their gentile state they are not subject to the halakhot of inheritance.

notes.dh: דבהיותו עובד כוכבים לאו בני נחלה נינהו
notes.he: פירש בקונטרס עובדי כוכבים אינם בני נחלה משנתגיירו ובפרק קמא דקדושין (דף יז:) משמע דהם בני נחלה דאמרינן בקדושין דעובד כוכבים יורש את אביו דבר תורה אלא לאו בני נחלה נינהו דקאמר הכא היינו תורת בכורה:
notes.en: Because in their gentile state they are not subject to inheritance: Rashi explained that gentiles are not heirs once they have converted. But the first chapter of Kiddushin (17b) implies that they are heirs, for we say there that a gentile inherits his father by Torah law. Rather, “they are not subject to inheritance” here means [they are not subject to] the law of the firstborn.

notes.dh: בגיותן לאו בני נחלה נינהו דאין אב לעובד כוכבים
notes.he: לישנא אחרינא כדאמר במס' קידושין נכרי את הגר וגר את הגר אינו לא מד"ת ולא מד"ס דתניא לוה מעות מן הגר שנתגיירו בניו עמו כו' משום הכי יש לו בכור לנחלה:
notes.en: In their gentile state they are not subject to inheritance: since a gentile has no [legal] father. Another explanation: as it says in tractate Kiddushin, a gentile [inheriting] from a convert, or a convert from a convert, is [an heir] neither by Torah law nor by rabbinic law, as it is taught: one who borrowed money from a convert whose sons converted with him, etc. That is why he has a firstborn for inheritance.

messages.text: But with regard to that case, the mitzva to be fruitful and multiply, say he concedes to Rabbi Yoḥanan that since the verse states: “He did not create it to be a waste; He formed it to be inhabited,” and he has indeed performed an action that enables the world to be further inhabited, he has therefore fulfilled the mitzva.

notes.he: בפ' הבא על יבמתו (יבמות דף סב.) קאמר בלשון אחר דמעיקרא נמי בני פריה ורביה נינהו ולאו בני חיוב קאמר דבפ' ד' מיתות (סנהדרין דף נט:) מוכח דלא מיפקדא אפריה ורביה אלא כלומר דזרעו מתייחס אחריו והיינו עבד ליה שבת דקאמר הכא וגבי עבד קאמר ביבמות (דף סב.) דהכל מודים דאין לו חייס:
notes.en: And he has indeed performed [what makes the world] inhabited: In chapter HaBa al Yevimto (Yevamot 62a) it says, in other words, that even beforehand [as gentiles] they are subject to being fruitful and multiplying. That does not mean they are obligated, for chapter Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 59b) shows that they were not commanded to be fruitful and multiply. Rather, it means that his offspring is traced after him, and that is what “he has performed inhabitation” means here. And concerning a slave it says in Yevamot (62a) that all agree he has no lineage [ḥayis].

notes.he: והא עבד ליה שבת בנים:
notes.en: And he has indeed performed inhabitation: [through his] sons.

messages.text: And conversely, if their dispute were stated only with regard to this mitzva to be fruitful and multiply, perhaps it is only in this case that Rabbi Yoḥanan says his opinion, due to the verse: “He formed it to be inhabited.” But with regard to that case of inheritance, say he concedes to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish that sons born when one was a gentile are disregarded. Consequently, it is necessary to teach their opinions in both disputes.
The Gemara raises a difficulty concerning the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan: We learned in the mishna:

One who did not have sons and he married a woman who had already given birth; or if he married a woman who gave birth when she was still a Canaanite maidservant and she was then emancipated; or one who gave birth when she was still a gentile and she then converted, and when the maidservant or the gentile came to join the Jewish people she gave birth to a male, that offspring is a firstborn with regard to inheritance but is not a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest.

notes.dh: מי שלא היו לו בנים כו'
notes.he: פרישית לעיל גבי מתני':
notes.en: One who did not have sons, etc.: I explained it above, at the mishna [46a].

messages.text: This maidservant or convert, whose child that was born when she came to join the Jewish people is a firstborn for inheritance, from whom, i.e., from what type of father, did she bear him?
messages.quote: when the maidservant or the gentile came to join the Jewish people she gave birth

notes.he: דקתני משבאה לישראל ילדה הוי בכור לנחלה:
notes.en: From whom did she give birth: since it teaches that once she came to join the Jewish people she gave birth [to a son who] is a firstborn for inheritance.

notes.he: כלומר הא דתני משבאת לישראל ילדה ממאן ילדה:
notes.en: From whom did she give birth: that is, this that it teaches, “once she came to join the Jewish people she gave birth”: from whom did she give birth?

messages.text: If we say she bore him from a Jew who did not previously have sons, the initial subject of this clause of the mishna, why does it make reference specifically to a gentile or a maidservant, indicating that this son is a firstborn for inheritance because the ones born when she was not Jewish are disregarded? The halakha would be the same even with regard to a Jewish woman who had already given birth.

notes.he: דמשמע מש"ה הוי בכור לנחלה דאותם בנים שהיו לה בהיותה עובדת כוכבים לא חשיבי:
notes.en: Why specifically a convert or a maidservant: this implies that he is a firstborn for inheritance for that reason, because the sons she had in her gentile state do not count.

notes.he: דבנים הראשונים חשובים בנים הוי האי נמי בכור לנחלה דהא באב תליא מילתא ולא באם:
notes.en: Even a Jewish woman as well: even if her first sons count as sons, this one would still be a firstborn for inheritance, for the matter depends on the father and not on the mother.

notes.he: דהוי בכור לנחלה אפי' בת ישראל נמי בכור לנחלה הוי:
notes.en: Why specifically a convert or a maidservant, that he is a firstborn for inheritance? Even [with] a Jewish woman he would be a firstborn for inheritance.

messages.text: Rather, is the mishna not referring to two distinct cases? The first concerns a man who already had children before converting, and then marries a Jew who has already given birth to children, while the second involves a woman who had children when she was a maidservant or a gentile, and when she became Jewish she bore a child from one like her, a convert who had sons when he was a gentile and then converted. And the mishna teaches that this son is a firstborn with regard to inheritance, which apparently contradicts the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan.

notes.he: האי ילדה משבאה לישראל לא אמי שלא היו לו בנים מהדר אלא מילתא באפי נפשה היא דקאמר גיורת שהיו לה בנים בהיותה עובדת כוכבים ונתגיירה עם בעלה וילדה משבאתה לתורת ישראל הוי בכור לנחלה ותיובתא דר' יוחנן:
notes.en: Rather, is it not: this “once she came to join the Jewish people she gave birth” does not go back to “one who did not have sons.” Rather, it is a separate case: a convert who had sons in her gentile state and converted together with her husband, and gave birth once she came under the law of Israel; [her son] is a firstborn for inheritance. And this is a refutation of Rabbi Yoḥanan.

notes.he: אע"ג דכבר הוליד בנים בגיותו ותיובתא דרבי יוחנן דאמר היו לו בנים בגיותו אין לו בכור לנחלה:
notes.en: And it teaches “a firstborn for inheritance,” even though he already fathered sons in his gentile state. This is a refutation of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who said that if he had sons in his gentile state he has no firstborn for inheritance.

messages.text: No; actually, her child was born from a Jew who did not have sons, and the reason the mishna makes reference specifically to a gentile or a maidservant is not due to the case of inheritance. Rather, it was necessary for the clause: But is not a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest.
messages.quote: but is not a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest

notes.dh: לעולם מישראל שלא היו לו בנים
notes.he: ומשום בכור לנחלה לא איצטריך למינקט גיורת אלא משום דאשמעינן דאינו בכור לכהן דבנים הראשונים מיקרו פטר רחם ולאפוקי מדר' יוסי הגלילי:
notes.en: Actually, from a Jew who did not have sons: for the sake of “a firstborn for inheritance” there was no need to mention a convert. Rather, [it is mentioned] because it teaches us that he is not a firstborn for the priest, since the earlier sons are called “opening the womb”; and [this is] to exclude [the view] of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

messages.text: This statement serves to exclude the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who says:

That son is a firstborn with regard to inheritance and with regard to redemption from a priest, as it is stated: “Whatever opens the womb among the children of Israel” (Exodus 13:2), i.e., one is not considered a firstborn unless he opens the womb of a woman from the Jewish people, and therefore the children that she bore before she converted are not considered to have opened her womb.

verse.he: קַדֶּשׁ־לִי כׇל־בְּכוֹר פֶּטֶר כׇּל־רֶחֶם בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה לִי הוּא׃
verse.en: “Consecrate to Me every male first-born; human and animal, the first [male] issue of every womb among the Israelites is Mine.”

messages.text: Therefore, the first tanna of the mishna teaches us that he is not a firstborn with regard to redemption, as his mother’s womb was already opened when she was a gentile.

notes.he: (רבי יוחנן) [מתניתין] דלא הוי בכור לכהן אלא בכור לנחלה:
notes.en: It teaches us: [the printed text reads “Rabbi Yoḥanan” here, corrected in brackets to “our mishna”] that he is not a firstborn for the priest, only a firstborn for inheritance.

messages.text: Come and hear a proof against Rabbi Yoḥanan from a baraita:
If a man had sons when he was a gentile and he converted, and then fathered more sons, he has a firstborn with regard to inheritance.

This ruling is certainly in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who says that the phrase in the verse “whatever opens the womb among the children of Israel” means it is not a firstborn unless it opens the womb of a woman from the Jewish people. And he derives his halakha, that of a gentile who converted, from her halakha, that of a female convert, that one does not take into account the children born before they converted. Rabbi Yoḥanan may hold in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who disagree with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.
messages.quote: he has a firstborn with regard to inheritance

notes.he: דקתני בכור לנחלה רבי יוסי הגלילי היא דלגבי כהן חשיב ליה בכור דעד שיפטרו רחם בישראל:
notes.en: This: [the baraita] that teaches “a firstborn for inheritance” is Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who counts him a firstborn with respect to the priest, [reading the verse as] “until they open a womb in Israel.”

notes.he: הבעל:
notes.en: And he derives: the husband.

notes.he: כי היכי דלגבה לא חשיבי בנים ראשונים והוי האי פטר רחם דכתיב בישראל לגביה נמי לא חשיבי ראשונים והוי האי ראשית אונו:
notes.en: From her: just as for her the earlier sons do not count, and this one is the “opening of the womb” written “in Israel,” so for him too the earlier ones do not count, and this one is “the first of his strength.”

notes.he: הגר מינה דידה דגיורת מה היא לטעמיה דר' יוסי אע"ג דהיו לו בנים בגיותה דיש לו בכור לנחלה:
notes.en: And he derives: the [male] convert [derives] from her, the female convert. Just as for her, according to Rabbi Yosei, even though she had sons, [her son] is a firstborn for the priest, so too for him, even though he had sons [in his gentile state], he has a firstborn for inheritance. [We follow the correction printed in the text; the uncorrected wording is garbled.]

messages.text: With regard to the daughter of a Levite who gave birth to a firstborn boy, her son is exempt from the obligation to give five sela coins to the priest for his redemption, as the child is considered to be the son of a Levite and Levites are exempt from this obligation.

notes.he: בת לוי:
notes.en: Leviyya: the daughter of a Levite.

messages.text: From whom did she become pregnant? If we say that she became pregnant from a priest or a Levite, why does Rav Adda bar Ahava refer specifically to the daughter of a Levite? The halakha would be the same even for an Israelite woman who became pregnant from a priest or a Levite.
messages.quote: the daughter of a Levite who gave birth

notes.he: דאמרן בפירקין קמא (דף ג:) הכהנים והלוים פטורין:
notes.en: Even an Israelite woman as well: as we said in the first chapter (3b), priests and Levites are exempt.

messages.text: Rather, Rav Adda bar Ahava must be referring to a case where the daughter of a Levite became pregnant from an Israelite. But if so, why is the son’s status determined by his mother’s status in this instance? After all, it is written: “By their families, by their fathers’ houses” (Numbers 1:2), which indicates that the lineage of a Jewish family follows the father rather than the mother.

verse.he: שְׂאוּ אֶת־רֹאשׁ כׇּל־עֲדַת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם לְבֵית אֲבֹתָם בְּמִסְפַּר שֵׁמוֹת כׇּל־זָכָר לְגֻלְגְּלֹתָם׃
verse.en: Take a census of the whole Israelite community by the clans of its ancestral houses, listing the names, every male, head by head.

notes.he: דמשפחת אב נפקא מהכא דקרויה משפחה ולא משפחת אם ואמאי פטור:
notes.en: By their fathers’ houses: from here we learn that the father’s family is called “family,” and not the mother’s family. So why is he exempt?

notes.he: דמשפחת אב קרויה משפחה ואמאי פטורה:
notes.en: “By their families, by their fathers’ houses” is written: the father’s family is called “family.” So why is she [her son] exempt?

messages.text: This is referring to the daughter of a Levite who became pregnant from a gentile. In such a case, the son’s status is determined by that of the mother, and therefore the son is exempt from the redemption of the firstborn.

notes.he: דל"ל חייס לגבי ישראל ושייך הבן בתר אם ישראלית טפי מבתר אבוה עובד כוכבים הלכך פטור:
notes.en: Who became pregnant from a gentile: since [a gentile] has no lineage [ḥayis] with regard to Jews, the son belongs to his Jewish mother more than to his gentile father; therefore he is exempt.

messages.text: And do not say this is the halakha only according to the one who says that in such a situation one does not disqualify the child at all due to his gentile father, and he is of fit lineage. Rather, even according to the one who says that one does disqualify the child due to the gentile father, nevertheless, one also follows the mother and he is therefore called a Levite of flawed lineage, and is exempt from redemption.

notes.dh: ולא תימא אליבא דמ"ד אין מזהמין את הולד
notes.he: במס' יבמות (דף מה.) דאיכא למ"ד עובד כוכבים הבא על בת ישראל הוולד כשר דבתר אימיה שדינן ליה ומשום הכי פטור מחמש סלעים:
notes.en: And do not say [it is] according to the one who says one does not disqualify the child: in tractate Yevamot (45a), where one opinion holds that if a gentile has intercourse with a Jewish woman the child is fit, since we assign him to his mother; and for that reason he would be exempt from the five sela.

notes.he: דשדינן ליה בתר עובד כוכבים אפ"ה פטור דלוי פסול מיקרי הואיל ואית ליה שמא דלוי פטור:
notes.en: Rather, even according to the one who says one does disqualify [the child]: that we assign him to the gentile; even so he is exempt, for he is called a flawed Levite. Since he bears the name Levite, he is exempt.

notes.dh: ולא תימא אליבא דמ"ד אין מזהמין כו'
notes.he: ומ"ד מזהמין היינו מאן דשדי ליה בתר עובד כוכבים כדפי' בקונט' דקרי ליה מזהמין משום דעובדי כוכבים מזוהמין הם כדאמרן שבת (דף קמו.) בשעה שבא נחש על חוה הטיל בה זוהמא ולא פסקה זוהמא מן העובדי כוכבים ומ"ד עובד כוכבים ועבד הבא על בת ישראל הולד כשר שדי ליה בתר דעובד כוכבים אבל מ"ד הולד ממזר שדי ליה בתר בת ישראל ולהכי שייך ביה ממזרות ובקונטרס פירש איפכא וכמו שפירשתי מוכח בסוף פ"ק דיבמות (דף יז.) בחלח וחבור וגו' א"ר יוחנן וכולן לפסול כי אמריתא קמיה דשמואל א"ל [כי] יסיר את בנך מאחרי בנך הבא מישראלית קרוי בנך ואין בנך הבא מן העובדת כוכבים קרוי בנך אלא בנה פירוש לא מיפסלי כיון דמתייחס אחר העובדת כוכבים ובנות ישראל דההוא דרא איצטרויי איצטרי וכן מוכח בפ"ק דיבמות (שם) דהאי דקרי ליה בנך גורם לו ממזרות:
notes.en: In brief: The one who says “one disqualifies [mezahamin]” assigns the child to the gentile father, as Rashi explained; it is called “taint” because gentiles are tainted, as said in Shabbat (146a): when the serpent came upon Eve it cast taint into her, and the taint has not ceased from the gentiles. But [Tosafot hold that] the one who says the child of a gentile or slave and a Jewish woman is fit is the one who assigns him to the gentile, while the one who says the child is a mamzer assigns him to the Jewish mother, and that is why mamzer status can apply to him. Rashi explained it the other way around. Tosafot’s reading is shown at the end of the first chapter of Yevamot (17a): Rabbi Yoḥanan said [the exiled tribes’ descendants] are all disqualified; Shmuel answered from “For he will turn away your son” (Deuteronomy 7:4): your son from a Jewish woman is called your son, but your son from a gentile woman is not called your son but her son. That is, they are not disqualified, since such a child is traced after the gentile mother (and the Jewish women of that generation had become barren). So it is shown there that being called “your son” is what brings mamzer status. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: רב אדא דתני פטור היינו אליבא דמאן דאמר במס' יבמות אין מזהמין את הולד דעובד כוכבים ועבד הבא על בת ישראל אין הולד ממזר דלא שדינן ליה בתר אביו אלא בתר אימיה והאי נמי בתר אימיה לויה שדינן ליה דפטור מחמש סלעים אלא אפי' למ"ד מזהמין הולד מ"מ בתר אימיה שדינן ליה ולוי פסול מיקרי ופטור:
notes.en: And do not say: that Rav Adda, who teaches “exempt,” is [speaking] according to the one who says in tractate Yevamot that one does not disqualify the child: that when a gentile or a slave has intercourse with a Jewish woman the child is not a mamzer, since we do not assign him to his father but to his mother; and this one too we assign to his Levite mother, so he is exempt from five sela. Rather, even according to the one who says one disqualifies the child, we still assign him to his mother; he is called a flawed Levite and is exempt.

messages.text: Actually, Rav Adda bar Ahava is referring to a case where the daughter of a Levite became pregnant from an Israelite. And although the son’s status is usually determined by that of the father, there, with regard to the redemption of the firstborn, it is different, as the verse states: “Whatever opens the womb among the children of Israel” (Exodus 13:2). This teaches that the Merciful One renders the obligation dependent upon the opening of the womb, and since this firstborn came from the womb of a daughter of a Levite, and not a Levite, the obligation of redemption does not apply.
messages.quote: the daughter of a Levite who gave birth

verse.he: קַדֶּשׁ־לִי כׇל־בְּכוֹר פֶּטֶר כׇּל־רֶחֶם בִּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה לִי הוּא׃
verse.en: “Consecrate to Me every male first-born; human and animal, the first [male] issue of every womb among the Israelites is Mine.”

notes.he: אחר האם אזיל לענין ה' סלעים:
notes.en: On the opening of the womb: for the five sela, [the matter] goes after the mother.

notes.dh: מר בריה דרב יוסף משמיה דרבא [אמר] לעולם מישראל
notes.he: כוותיה פסקינן בחולין בריש הזרוע (חולין דף קלב.) ואהא סמכינן השתא לפטור בן לויה וכהנת אשת ישראל מחמש סלעים:
notes.en: Mar, son of Rav Yosef, said in the name of Rava: actually, from an Israelite: We rule in accordance with him in Ḥullin, at the beginning of [chapter] HaZero’a (132a), and on this we rely nowadays to exempt from the five sela the son of a Levite’s daughter or of a priest’s daughter who is married to an Israelite.

notes.he: באמו ואמו אתיא משבט פטור:
notes.en: The Merciful One made it depend on the opening of the womb: [that is,] on his mother, and his mother comes from an exempt tribe.

messages.text: The Gemara raises a difficulty concerning the opinion of Rav Pappa: We learned in the mishna:

One who had sons and married a woman who had not given birth; or a woman who converted while she was pregnant, or a Canaanite maidservant who was emancipated while she was pregnant and she gave birth to a son, he is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest but he is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance.

notes.he: פרישית לעיל גבי מתני'. מדקתני היא וכהנת רבותא אשמעינן דאע"ג דנתערב עם הפטור איהו חייב:
notes.en: One who had sons: I explained it above, at the mishna. From the fact that it teaches “she and a priest’s daughter,” it teaches us a novelty: even though he was mixed up with one who is exempt, he is obligated.

messages.text: And likewise, if an Israelite woman and the daughter or wife of a priest, neither of whom had given birth yet, or an Israelite woman and the daughter or wife of a Levite, or an Israelite woman and a woman who had already given birth, gave birth, and it is uncertain which son was born to which mother;

and likewise a woman who did not wait three months after the death of her husband and she married and gave birth, and it is unknown whether the child was born after nine months and is the son of the first husband, or whether he was born after seven months and is the son of the latter husband, in all these cases the child is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest but is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance.

From the ruling in the case of one whose child became confused with that of a daughter of a priest or a Levite, by inference one can derive that the daughter of a priest and the daughter of a Levite are exempt from redemption.
messages.quote: an Israelite woman and the daughter or wife of a priest

notes.he: וקס"ד דהא כהנת בבת כהן קאמר:
notes.en: By inference that a priest’s daughter is exempt: and we now assume that “kohenet” means the daughter of a priest.

notes.he: מדקתני ילדה היא וכהנת היא ולויה מכלל דכהנת ולויה שילדו פטורין:
notes.en: From the fact that it teaches “she gave birth, and a priest’s daughter, and a Levite’s daughter,” by inference a priest’s daughter and a Levite’s daughter who gave birth are exempt.

messages.text: Now, from whom did she become pregnant? If we say that she became pregnant from a priest or a Levite, if so, why specifically mention the daughter of a priest and the daughter of a Levite? The same halakha would apply even in the case of an Israelite woman who became pregnant from a priest or a Levite, as the son is exempt from redemption because he is also a priest or a Levite.
Rather, if the case is where the daughter of a priest or the daughter of a Levite became pregnant from a gentile, then is the son of the daughter of a priest exempt? But didn’t Rav Pappa say:
Rabba tested us on the following matter:

notes.he: מנסה אותנו בהלכות:
notes.en: Badik: he tests us on halakhot.

messages.text: With regard to the daughter of a priest who became pregnant from a gentile, what is the halakha?

notes.he: מי הוי בנה פטור מבכורה או לא:
notes.en: What is [the halakha]: is her son exempt from [the redemption of] the firstborn or not?

messages.text: @Rabba Isn’t this the case discussed by Rav Adda bar Ahava, who says: With regard to the daughter of a Levite who gave birth to a firstborn boy, her son is exempt from the obligation to give five sela coins? This ruling was interpreted as referring to one who became pregnant from a gentile.

notes.he: וכי היכי דלוייה פטורה כהנת נמי פטורה:
notes.en: Isn’t this [the case] of Rav Adda: and just as a Levite’s daughter is exempt, so a priest’s daughter is exempt.

notes.he: ולאו היינו דרב אדא דאמר לויה שילדה כו' ואוקימנא בדאיעבר מעובד כוכבים וכהנת נמי דאיעברא מעובד כוכבים פטורה:
notes.en: And isn’t this [the case] of Rav Adda, who said: a Levite’s daughter who gave birth, etc.? And we established it as where she became pregnant from a gentile. So a priest’s daughter who became pregnant from a gentile is also exempt.

messages.text: @Rav Pappa How can these cases be compared? Granted, if the daughter of a Levite has a child from a gentile, he is considered a Levite with regard to redemption since his mother retains her sanctity. As it is taught in a baraita:
messages.lead: Rav Pappa continues: And he said to me:

notes.he: אע"ג דנבעלה לעובד כוכבים וכי שדינן בנה בתרה הוי כלוי פסול ופטור:
notes.en: She retains her sanctity: even though she had intercourse with a gentile; and when we assign her son to her, he is like a flawed Levite and is exempt.

messages.text: In the case of a Levite woman who was captured, leading to a concern that one of her captors might have engaged in sexual intercourse with her, or even if a Levite woman definitely engaged in licentious sexual intercourse, one nevertheless gives her first tithe and she may eat it.

notes.he: מעשר ראשון ניתן ללוים:
notes.en: From the tithe: the first tithe is given to the Levites.

notes.he: אין חולקין לאשה בגורן אבל מחלקין להם בבתיהם כדאמר בפרק נושאין על האנוסה (יבמות דף צט:):
notes.en: One gives her tithe and she eats it: one does not give a share to a woman at the threshing floor, but one does distribute to them in their homes, as it says in chapter Nosin al HaAnusa (Yevamot 99b).

messages.text: But with regard to the daughter of a priest, since if a gentile engages in intercourse with her she becomes like a non-priest and may no longer partake of teruma, her son from a gentile should be considered like an Israelite and be obligated in the redemption of a firstborn.

notes.he: לעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: Once he has intercourse with her: the gentile.

notes.he: כדאמרינן ביבמות בפרק אלמנה לכהן גדול (יבמות דף סח.) מנין לכהנת לויה וישראלית שבאו עליה עובד כוכבים ועבד שפסלוה ת"ל ובת כהן כי תהיה לאיש זר כיון שנבעלה לפסול לה פסלה ואע"ג דלויה נמי קתני התם מתרומה דקא פסיל לה שלא תינשא לכהן אבל מדין לויה לא מיפסלא:
notes.en: She becomes a zara [non-priest]: as we say in Yevamot, chapter Almana LeKohen Gadol (68a): From where [do we learn] that a priest’s daughter, a Levite’s daughter and an Israelite’s daughter with whom a gentile or a slave had intercourse are disqualified? The verse states: “And if a priest’s daughter be married to a stranger [zar]” (Leviticus 22:12): once she has had intercourse with one who is unfit for her, he disqualifies her. And although the Levite’s daughter is also taught there, that is about teruma: he disqualifies her from marrying a priest. But from the status of a Levite’s daughter she is not disqualified.

notes.he: וכיון דזרה היא בנה חייב בה' סלעים. הלכך מתניתין נמי לא מוקמת דאיעבר מעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: She becomes a zara: and since she is a zara, her son is obligated in the five sela. Therefore the mishna, too, cannot be explained as where she became pregnant from a gentile.

notes.dh: אלא כהנת כיון דאיבעילה [ליה] הויא לה זרה
notes.he: ואפי' קדושת לויה פקעה מינה וגרעה מלויה אשת כהן שנשבית דאע"ג דמיפסלא מתרומה לא פקעה מינה קדושתה לענין ה' סלעים אבל כהנת דקדושתה מגופה אתיא כשמתחללת פקעה קדושתה לגמרי:
notes.en: But a priest’s daughter, once [a gentile] has had intercourse with her, becomes a zara: even the sanctity of a Levite’s daughter departs from her, and she is lower than a Levite woman married to a priest who was taken captive. That woman, although she is disqualified from teruma, does not lose her sanctity with respect to the five sela. But a priest’s daughter, whose sanctity comes from her own person, loses her sanctity entirely when she is profaned.

messages.text: If so, in what case does the mishna exempt the son of a daughter of a priest or a daughter of a Levite from redemption?

This works out well according to the opinion of Mar, son of Rav Yosef, citing in the name of Rava, who says that Rav Adda bar Ahava, who deems the son of a Levite woman exempt from the obligation of redemption, was referring to a case where she became pregnant from an Israelite. This is because he can interpret the mishna as referring to the daughter of a priest or the daughter of a Levite who became pregnant from an Israelite.
messages.quote: where the daughter of a Levite became pregnant from an Israelite

notes.he: דמוקים לדרב אדא בדאיעבר מישראל מוקמי למתני' נמי הכי:
notes.en: This works out well according to Mar, son of Rav Yosef: who explains Rav Adda’s ruling as where she became pregnant from an Israelite; he explains the mishna the same way.

messages.text: But according to the opinion of Rav Pappa, who maintains that the son of a priest’s or Levite’s daughter who became pregnant from an Israelite is subject to the obligation of redemption from a priest, with regard to what case does he interpret the mishna?

notes.he: אלא רב פפא דאוקים לה לעיל לויה בדאיעבר מעובד כוכבים והכא לא מצי לאוקומי בעובד כוכבים משום דקתני כהנת במאי מוקים לה:
notes.en: But Rav Pappa, who explained the Levite’s daughter above as where she became pregnant from a gentile, and here cannot explain it as a gentile because it teaches “a priest’s daughter”: how does he explain it?

messages.text: Actually, the mishna is not referring to the daughter of a priest but to a woman who became pregnant from a priest. Therefore, her son is exempt from redemption, and yet she herself is an Israelite woman. And why does the mishna call her the daughter of a priest [kohenet]? Because her son is a priest.

notes.he: מתניתין דאיעבר מכהן אבל בת כהן דלא איעבר מכהן לא מיפטרא דלא אזלינן בתר אם אלא בלויה דאיעבר מעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: Actually: the mishna is where she became pregnant from a priest. But a priest’s daughter who did not become pregnant from a priest is not exempt, for we follow the mother only for a Levite’s daughter who became pregnant from a gentile.

notes.he: כהנת דקתני בת ישראל היא ודאיעבר מכהן ואמאי קרי לה כהנת הואיל ובנה כהן:
notes.en: Actually: the “kohenet” it teaches is an Israelite woman who became pregnant from a priest. And why does it call her kohenet? Because her son is a priest.

messages.caption: Whose son is exempt from the five sela? The cases Rav Pappa and Mar, son of Rav Yosef, discuss on 47a.

messages.text: It was stated that in the case of a priest who married a divorcée and then died and left a son who was a priest disqualified due to flawed lineage [ḥalal] and has the status of a non-priest:

notes.he: כישראל דמי וחייב בבכורה:
notes.en: A ḥalal son: he is like an Israelite and is obligated in [the redemption of] the firstborn.

messages.text: The son is obligated to redeem himself.

notes.he: דהא לא זכה האב בפדיונו אלא חייב הבן לפדות עצמו אע"ג דליכא חיובא באב וכן מתני' דתנן נתגיירה מעוברת נשתחררה מעוברת (כשר) ותימה דבפ"ק דקדושין (דף כט.) גמרינן ממצות הבן על האב דדרשינן תפדה תפדה אשה שאין אחרים מצווין לפדותה אינה מצווה לפדות עצמה וה"נ האי בן שאין אחרים מצווין לפדותו לא יהא חייב לפדות עצמו וי"ל דלא דמי האי בן לאשה דלא שייך בה בשום אב פדיון כלל אבל הכא אם היה לו אב ישראל היה חייב לפדותו:
notes.en: The son is obligated to redeem himself: since the father did not acquire his redemption, the son is obligated to redeem himself even though there is no obligation on the father. So too the mishna that teaches “converted while pregnant, was freed while pregnant.” This is puzzling: in the first chapter of Kiddushin (29a) we derive from the father’s mitzva toward his son, expounding “tifdeh, tifdeh,” that a woman, whom others are not commanded to redeem, is not commanded to redeem herself. So too this son, whom others are not commanded to redeem, should not be obligated to redeem himself! One may answer that this son is not like a woman, for whom redemption does not apply through any father at all. But here, had he had an Israelite father, the father would have been obligated to redeem him.

notes.he: דהוי כזר וצריך לפדות עצמו:
notes.en: The son is obligated to redeem himself: for he is like a non-priest and must redeem himself.

messages.text: He is not obligated to redeem himself.

notes.dh: רבה בר רב הונא אמר אין הבן חייב לפדות עצמו
notes.he: שאביו זכה בפדיונו והוא יורש נכסי אביו והנכסים פטורין:
notes.en: Rabba bar Rav Huna said: The son is not obligated to redeem himself, for his father acquired his redemption, and he inherits his father’s property, and the property is exempt.

messages.text: In any case that the father died after thirty days following the birth of the son, at which point the father was already obligated in his redemption, everyone agrees that the son is not obligated to redeem himself, as his father acquired his redemption money, i.e., it is as though he separated five sela coins and took the money for himself, since he is a priest.

notes.he: ישנו במצות פדייה דכתיב (במדבר י״ח:ט״ו-ט״ז) ופדויו מבן חדש:
notes.en: After thirty [days]: [the father] is [then] subject to the mitzva of redemption, as it is written: “And their redemption money, from a month old” (Numbers 18:16).

notes.he: דאי נמי יהיב (ליה) האב הוה מפריש ליה ושקיל ליה לנפשיה דהא כהן הוא וכיון דזכה האב בפדיונו מורישו לבנו עם שאר נכסיו:
notes.en: For his father acquired his redemption: even if the father had given it, he would have separated it and taken it for himself, since he is a priest. And since the father acquired his redemption money, he bequeaths it to his son with the rest of his property.

messages.text: They disagree when the father died within thirty days of the birth of the son, before the obligation of redemption had taken effect.
The son is obligated to redeem himself, as his father did not acquire his redemption money.

notes.he: דהא לא איחייב אב מעולם אלא בן נתחייב לאחר מיתת אביו ואיחייב ליה למיתביה לכהן אחר:
notes.en: The father did not acquire: the father was never obligated; rather, the son became obligated after his father’s death, and he must give it to another priest.

messages.text: The son is not obligated to redeem himself, as he can say to a priest who demands the redemption money from him: I come due to the strength of a man with whom you cannot enter into judgment, i.e., if my father were alive he would have separated five sela coins and taken the money for himself, and I inherit his claim.

notes.he: האי חלל לכהן אתינא מכח גברא כהן דלא מצית אישתעויי דינא בהדיה שאם היה אביו פודה אותו היה נוטל הפדיון לעצמו:
notes.en: For he says to him: this ḥalal [says] to the priest: I come by the strength of a man, a priest, with whom you cannot enter into judgment, for had my father redeemed me he would have taken the redemption money for himself.

notes.dh: קא אתינא מכח גברא דלא מצית משתעי דינא בהדיה
notes.he: דאילו הוה אבא קיים לא מצית למיתבעיה דאי בתוך שלשים אכתי לא איחייב ואי לאחר שלשים איהו זכה בפדיונו שהרי הוא כהן הלכך אנא דאתינא מכחיה פטירנא:
notes.en: I come by the strength of a man with whom you cannot enter into judgment: for if my father were alive you could not claim it from him. If within thirty [days], he was not yet obligated; and if after thirty, he acquired his redemption money, since he is a priest. Therefore I, who come by his strength, am exempt.

messages.text: The Gemara raises a challenge to the opinion of Rabba bar Rav Huna: We learned in the mishna: If one married a woman who converted while she was pregnant, having been impregnated by a gentile, the child is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest and must redeem himself.
messages.quote: I come due to the strength of a man with whom you cannot enter into judgment

notes.he: ולא ילדה עדיין מעולם אותו וולד בכור לכהן:
notes.en: Converted while pregnant: and she had never given birth before; that child is a firstborn for the priest.

messages.text: But why is this the halakha? Let this son say to the priest: I come due to the strength of a man with whom you cannot enter into judgment, as his father is a gentile, from whom the redemption money cannot be claimed.

notes.dh: אמאי לימא ליה אתינא מכח גברא
notes.he: דלא ציית דינא:
notes.en: Why? Let him say to him: I come by the strength of a man: who does not heed judgment.

notes.dh: לימא ליה קא אתינא מכח גברא
notes.he: מכח עובד כוכבים דלא איחייב:
notes.en: Let him say to him: I come by the strength of a man: by the strength of a gentile, who was not obligated.

messages.text: The case of a gentile is different, as he has no lineage [ḥayis], i.e., this man is not considered his father’s son at all.

notes.he: לגבי ישראל לית ליה שום יחס ואין זה בא מכחו דכקטן שנולד דמי:
notes.en: Who has no lineage [ḥayis]: with regard to Jews he has no lineage at all, and this one does not come by his strength, for [a convert] is like a newborn child.

notes.he: שאני הכא מש"ה הוי בכור לכהן דעובד כוכבים לית ליה חייס דאין אב לעובד כוכבים:
notes.en: It is different here: that is why he is a firstborn for the priest, for a gentile has no ḥayis; a gentile has no [legal] father.

messages.text: With regard to a priest who died within thirty days of the birth of his son and left a son who was a ḥalal, the son is obligated to redeem himself, as the father did not acquire his redemption money. If the father died after thirty days following the birth of the son, the son is not obligated to redeem himself, as his father already acquired his redemption money.
messages.lead: On this matter, the Gemara notes that Rabbi Shimon Yasinia says that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says, in accordance with the opinion of Rav Ḥisda:

messages.text: …and she married and gave birth and it is unknown whether the son was born after a pregnancy of nine months and is the son of the first husband, or after seven months and is the son of the second husband, the son is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest but is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance.
messages.quote: And likewise a woman who did not wait three months after the death of her husband

messages.text: This son is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance, but he takes a share of the inheritance like an ordinary son. But why is he entitled to any inheritance? Let him go to that son of the first husband and he will reject him, by demanding proof that he is from his family, and likewise let him go to that son of the second husband and he will reject him in the same manner.

notes.he: דבנים של ראשון מצו מדחו ליה ולמימר ליה דשל אחרון הוית ובניו של אחרון מצי אמרו ליה בן של ראשון הוית:
notes.en: Let him go to this one and he will reject him: the first [husband’s] sons can reject him and say to him, “You are the latter’s”; and the latter’s sons can say to him, “You are the first one’s son.”

messages.text: This ruling that he is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance is necessary only with regard to the son who follows him, born to the second husband, to teach that he is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance, as this son of uncertain status might be his firstborn brother.

notes.he: מתני' דקתני אינו בכור לנחלה אלא מההוא שבא אחריו אלא איהו לא שקיל מידי דבנו הראשון אומר לו לא בן ראשון אתה וכן בנו האחרון אומר לו:
notes.en: It is necessary only: the mishna that teaches “is not a firstborn for inheritance” refers only to the one who comes after him. He himself takes nothing, for the first [husband’s] son says to him, “You are not the son of the first,” and so too the latter’s son says to him.

messages.text: And when the mishna states: The child is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest but is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance, this is what it is saying: This son of uncertain status is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest, and the son who follows him, born to the second husband, is not a firstborn with regard to inheritance.

notes.he: הוי האי ספק ממה נפשך דהאי פטר רחם הוא וחייב לפדות את עצמו והבא אחריו (מבני) השני אינו בכור לנחלה דאמרין ליה אחיו אותו ספק בן אבינו הוא ואתה אינך בכור:
notes.en: And this is what it is saying: [he is] a firstborn for the priest, this uncertain one, either way, since he opened the womb and is obligated to redeem himself. And the one who comes after him, [the son] of the second [husband], is not a firstborn for inheritance, for his brothers say to him: that uncertain one is [perhaps] our father’s son, and you are not the firstborn.

notes.he: אין ודאי האי מצי למידחייה אלא לא נצרכה למיתני אלא לבא אחריו וה"ק איהו ספק בן תשעה לראשון ספק בן ז' לאחרון ודאי בכור לכהן הוא דפטר רחם הוא. (והוא) והבא אחריו אינו בכור לא לנחלה דמצי אחי למידחייה ולא לכהן [דאינו פטר רחם]:
notes.en: Rabbi Yirmeya said: this one can indeed be rejected; the mishna was needed only for the one who comes after him. And this is what it says: he, uncertainly a nine-month [son] of the first and uncertainly a seven-month [son] of the latter, is certainly a firstborn for the priest, since he opened the womb. And the one who comes after him is not a firstborn, neither for inheritance, since his brothers can reject him, nor for the priest, [since he did not open the womb].

messages.text: And let the son with uncertain status and the son who follows him write an authorization to one another, by which each grants the other the right to claim his own share. In this manner they can claim the double portion together, as one of them is certainly the firstborn.

notes.he: הספק והבא אחריו יכתוב אחד הרשאה לחבירו על חלקו וילך ויתבע לו הבכורה ממה נפשך אם אני בכור תנו לי בשביל עצמי ואם אחי בכור תנו לי בשביל אחי דהא או הספק או הבא אחריו בכור:
notes.en: And let them write an authorization to one another: the uncertain one and the one after him; each writes the other an authorization for his share, and he goes and claims the firstborn’s portion either way: “If I am the firstborn, give it to me for myself; and if my brother is the firstborn, give it to me for my brother,” for either the uncertain one or the one after him is the firstborn.

notes.he: ואמאי אינו בכור לנחלה לא זה ולא זה וליכתבו הרשאה להדדי האי ספק להאי הבא אחריו והאי להאי וליתבעוה לאחיה ממה נפשך דאי בכור אנא הבו לי חלק בכורה. ואי לאו בכור אנא דאנא בריה דראשון הבו לי בשביל אחי הבא אחרי שהרי הירשני לקבל ואידך נמי לימא הכי:
notes.en: So why is neither this one nor that one a firstborn for inheritance? Let them write authorizations to each other, the uncertain one to the one who comes after him and he to him, and claim from their brothers either way: “If I am the firstborn, give me the firstborn’s portion; and if I am not the firstborn, since I am the first [husband’s] son, give it to me for my brother who came after me, since he authorized me to receive it.” And the other says the same.

messages.text: And if you would say that the mishna is dealing with a case where there was no authorization, we interpret it later on (see 49a) as referring to a situation where there was an authorization.

notes.he: מיירי והכי קאמר אם לא כתבו הרשאות אין כאן בכור לנחלה:
notes.en: And if you would say the mishna is dealing with [a case] without authorization: and this is what it says: if they did not write authorizations, there is no firstborn for inheritance.

notes.dh: הא מוקמינן ליה לקמן דבהרשאה קמיירי
notes.he: דאמר אמר שמואל בבא בהרשאה אלא ודאי הרשאה לא מהניא כלל הכא:
notes.en: But we explain it later on as dealing with an authorization: for it says there, “Shmuel said: [they come] with an authorization.” Rather, it must be that authorization does not help at all here.

notes.dh: וכי תימא מתניתין דקתני ואינו בכור לנחלה שלא בהרשאה קא מיירי
notes.he: והא מוקמינן לה מתניתין לקמן דקתני אם לכהן אחר נתנו יחזיר להן חמש סלעים משום דבאין עליו בהרשאה:
notes.en: And if you would say the mishna that teaches “and is not a firstborn for inheritance” deals with [a case] without authorization: but we explain the mishna below, which teaches “if he gave it to another priest, he must return the five sela to them,” as because they come against him with an authorization.

messages.text: The mishna, which indicates that there is no firstborn with regard to inheritance here, supports the opinion of Rabbi Yannai, as Rabbi Yannai says:

In a case where two sons of two men became confused and it is unknown who is the father of whom, if the two sons were initially recognized and were ultimately intermingled, each writes an authorization to the other, and the other sons in each family cannot claim that these sons are not their brother.

notes.dh: מסייע ליה לרבי ינאי דאמר הוכרו ולבסוף נתערבו
notes.he: כגון שתי נשים של שני אנשים שהוכרו וולדותיהן ואחר כך נתערבו ועכשיו כשהן באין כולן לירש דוחין אותן אחיהם דלכל אחד אמרי לאו אחינו אתה:
notes.en: This supports Rabbi Yannai, who said: they were recognized and in the end intermingled: for example, two wives of two men whose children were recognized and afterward became intermingled. Now, when they all come to inherit, their brothers reject them, saying to each one, “You are not our brother.”

notes.he: האחד לחבירו על חלקו בנכסי אביו ובעל ההרשאה בא אצל יורשי שני האבות ואומר לכל אחד אם אחיכם אני תנו לי ואם זה אחיכם תנו לי חלקו וכן לבני השני. אבל לא הוכרו מעולם אין כותבין דלא היתה להם זכיה מעולם בנכסי [אביו] ומתני' נמי בדלא הוכרו מעולם דמעולם לא נודע איזה בכור ולא זכה אחד מהם בחזקת בכורה. הא דרבי ינאי בב"ב ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכז.):
notes.en: They write an authorization to each other: each to the other for his share in his father’s property. The holder of the authorization comes to the heirs of each of the two fathers and says to each, “If I am your brother, give me [my share]; and if this one is your brother, give me his share”; and likewise to the second man’s sons. But if they were never recognized, they do not write, since they never had any entitlement to [their father’s] property. And the mishna too is where they were never recognized, since it was never known which one is the firstborn, and neither of them ever held the presumptive status of firstborn. This teaching of Rabbi Yannai is in Bava Batra, [chapter] Yesh Noḥalin (127a).

messages.text: If they were not initially recognized and were ultimately intermingled, each does not write an authorization to the other, as even initially neither of them had any certain right to their father’s inheritance.

Likewise, in the case of the uncertain son and the one who follows him in the mishna, neither one was ever recognized as his father’s firstborn. Therefore, writing an authorization is ineffective in claiming any inheritance.

notes.he: דהכא לא הוכרו מעולם האי ספק להכי אין כותבין הרשאה:
notes.en: This supports Rabbi Yannai: for here this uncertain one was never recognized; therefore they do not write an authorization.

messages.text: Mishna
Which is the offspring that is a firstborn both with regard to inheritance and with regard to redemption from a priest?

In the case of a woman who miscarried a gestational sac full of water, or one full of blood, or one full of pieces of flesh; or one who miscarries a mass resembling a fish, or grasshoppers, or repugnant creatures, or creeping animals, or one who miscarries on the fortieth day after conception, the son who follows any of them is a firstborn with regard to inheritance and with regard to redemption from a priest.

notes.he: עור הולד ממש:
notes.en: Mishna. Shafir: the actual skin of the fetus.

notes.he: גוונים:
notes.en: Genunim: colors. [The Davidson English renders genunim as “pieces of flesh.”]

notes.he: לאו וולד נינהו. וטעמא מפרש במס' נדה בהמפלת חתיכה (נדה דף כב:) שלא נאמרה בהן יצירה כלגבי אדם:
notes.en: And grasshoppers: these are not offspring. The reason is explained in tractate Nidda, [chapter] HaMapelet Ḥatikha (22b): “formation” is not said of them as it is of a human.

notes.he: שנתעברה דמיא בעלמא הוא עד דמטי למחר דמ' יום הוי יצירת הוולד:
notes.en: On the fortieth day: from conception. It is mere water until the day after the fortieth, for after forty days is the formation of the fetus.

notes.he: גוונים סרוחים. דלא הוי מרוקם לוולד:
notes.en: Full of genunim: putrid colors, which are not formed into a fetus.

notes.he: דאכתי לא איגמרא צורה:
notes.en: And one who miscarries on the fortieth day: for its form is not yet complete.

messages.text: In the case of a boy born by caesarean section and the son who follows him, both of them are not firstborn, neither with regard to inheritance nor with regard to redemption from a priest.

notes.he: דרך רחם שניהן אינן בכור וטעמא מפרש בגמרא:
notes.en: One born by caesarean section and the one after him: [who comes out] by way of the womb; neither of them is a firstborn, and the reason is explained in the Gemara.

messages.text: The first son is a firstborn with regard to inheritance if he is his father’s first son, and the second son is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest for five sela coins, because he is the first to emerge from the womb and he emerged in the usual way.
Gemara

The first son, born by caesarean section, is not considered the firstborn with regard to inheritance, as we require fulfillment of the verse: “And they have borne him children” (Deuteronomy 21:15), written in the context of inheritance, and a caesarean section is not called a birth.
messages.quote: born by caesarean section and the son who follows him, both of them are not firstborn

verse.he: כִּי־תִהְיֶיןָ לְאִישׁ שְׁתֵּי נָשִׁים הָאַחַת אֲהוּבָה וְהָאַחַת שְׂנוּאָה וְיָלְדוּ־לוֹ בָנִים הָאֲהוּבָה וְהַשְּׂנוּאָה וְהָיָה הַבֵּן הַבְּכֹר לַשְּׂנִיאָה׃
verse.en: If a man has two wives, one loved and the other unloved, and both the loved and the unloved have borne him sons, but the first-born is the son of the unloved one—

notes.he: דרך לידה:
notes.en: Gemara. We require “and they have borne him”: by way of birth.

notes.dh: ראשון לנחלה לא וילדו לו בעינן
notes.he: מתוך פירוש הקונטרס משמע דמלשון לידה גמר וקשה דבנדה [ריש] פרק יוצא דופן (נדה דף מ.) (ברישי') מפרש דאין יושבין עליו ימי טומאה וימי טהרה משום דכתיב אשה כי תזריע וילדה זכר עד שתלד ממקום שמזרעת אבל מלשון לידה לא אלא יש לפרש דגמר הכא לידה [לידה] מהתם ור"ש דהכא לטעמיה כדאמר בסמוך דמרבי התם יוצא דופן (שם) מתלד דיושבין עליו ימי טומאה וימי טהרה וא"ת דהתם קאמר דמודה ר"ש לענין קדשים שאינו קדוש דגמר מבכור דכתיב ביה פטר רחם ופריך וליגמר לידה לידה מאדם דמרבינן יוצא דופן מתלד שכן פשוט קדוש זכר במתנות ומשני מבכור אית לן למילף דנפישין שכן אמו בהמות קדשים פגול נותר וטמא והשתא הכא נמי נילף מבכור בהמה שכן בכור מבכור וי"ל דאינך נפישי שכן אדם מאדם ואינם קדושים ולא שייך בהם פגול נותר וטמא ובכור אדם דכהונה דכתיב ביה פטר רחם לא מצי ר"ש למילף מבכור לנחלה דגבי בכור אדם דפטר רחם לא כתיב לידה:
notes.en: In brief: Rashi’s explanation implies that [the Gemara] derives this from the word “birth” itself. This is difficult, for in Nidda, at the beginning of chapter Yotzei Dofen (40a), [the Gemara] explains that a woman does not observe days of impurity and purity for a caesarean birth because it is written “If a woman conceives and bears a male” (Leviticus 12:2): only when she bears from the place where she conceives; not from the word “birth.” Rather, one may explain that here it derives “birth” from “birth” [a verbal analogy] with that verse, and Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning, as stated below, for he includes a caesarean there from “she bears.” And if you say: it says there that Rabbi Shimon concedes that a caesarean consecrated animal is not sacred, because he derives it from the firstborn, where “opening the womb” is written; and the Gemara asks why not derive “birth” from “birth” from a human, and answers that the firstborn is the better source because it shares more features [with consecrated animals: both are animals, sacred, and subject to piggul, notar and impurity]. So here too, let us derive [the human firstborn for inheritance] from the animal firstborn! One may answer that the other features weigh more: a human from a human, and humans are not sacred, and piggul, notar and impurity do not apply to them. And as for the human firstborn of the priesthood, where “opening the womb” is written, Rabbi Shimon cannot derive it from the firstborn for inheritance, since “birth” is not written of the human firstborn who opens the womb. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: תימה כיון דדרשינן קרא בבכור א"כ בפרק יש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכז.) דדרשינן טומטום שנקרע ונמצא זכר דאינו ממעט בחלק בכורה דאמר קרא וילדו לו בנים עד שיהא בן משעת לידה והאי דאינו נוטל פי שנים דריש מוהיה הבכור עד שיהא בן משעת הווייה וכן בפ' מי שמת (בבא בתרא דף קמב:) דנן בן שנולד לאחר מיתת אביו דאינו ממעט מחלק בכורה מדכתיב וילדו לו והא דאינו נוטל פי שנים דריש מדכתיב יכיר ואמאי כולהו מילתא תיפוק ליה מוילדו לו כיון דמוקמינן ליה בבכור וי"ל דאי לאו דכתיבי תרי קראי הוה מוקמינן ליה דוקא בבכור דאינו נוטל פי שנים דהיה מסתבר לאוקמי טפי בבכור שלא יטול חלק בבכורה מלהעמידו בפשוט שלא ימעט בחלק בכורה תדע דביוצא דופן דליכא תרי קראי דרשינן ליה לענין דאינו נוטל פי שנים ולא דרשינן ליה לומר דאינו ממעט:
notes.en: In brief: If we apply “and they have borne him” to the firstborn, it is puzzling. In Bava Batra, chapter Yesh Noḥalin (127a), a tumtum who was torn open and found to be male does not reduce the firstborn’s portion, because the verse says “and they have borne him sons,” until he is a son from the moment of birth; and that he does not himself take a double portion is expounded from “and the firstborn son be,” until he is [a son] from the moment of being. Likewise in chapter Mi SheMet (Bava Batra 142b), a son born after his father’s death does not reduce the firstborn’s portion, from “and they have borne him,” and that he does not take a double portion is expounded from “he shall recognize.” Why not derive all of these from “and they have borne him,” since we apply it to the firstborn? One may answer: were it not that two verses are written, we would have applied it only to the firstborn, that he does not take a double portion, since that is more reasonable than applying it to an ordinary son, that he does not reduce the firstborn’s portion. Proof: for a caesarean, where there are not two verses, we expound it to mean that he does not take a double portion, and not that he does not reduce it. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: דרך לידה בעינן ויוצא דופן לא הוי לידה:
notes.en: And they have borne him: we require [birth] by way of birth, and a caesarean is not a birth.

messages.text: Likewise, with regard to the redemption with five sela coins, this son is also not considered the firstborn, as we require fulfillment of the verse: “Whatever opens the womb” (Exodus 13:2), and he did not open his mother’s womb.

Similarly, the second son who follows him is not considered the firstborn with regard to inheritance, as we require fulfillment of the verse: “For he is the first of his strength, the right of the firstborn is his” (Deuteronomy 21:17), and this son is not the first.

In addition, he is also not considered the firstborn with regard to the redemption of five sela coins, as the tanna of the mishna holds: A firstborn for only one matter, i.e., he opened his mother’s womb but is not her first child, is not considered a firstborn with regard to redemption.

notes.he: כגון זה שהוא בכור לרחמים ואינו בכור לוולדות דהא הוה לו ולד זכר קודם לו:
notes.en: A firstborn for one matter: such as this one, who is a firstborn of the womb but not a firstborn among the children, for there was a male child before him.

notes.he: לרחמים גרידא:
notes.en: A firstborn for one matter: of the womb alone.

messages.text: The verse states: “And they have borne him children,” and a caesarean section is not called a birth. Rabbi Shimon conforms to his standard line of reasoning, as he says with regard to a verse that deals with the ritual impurity of a woman after childbirth:
messages.lead: The mishna teaches that Rabbi Shimon says: The first son is a firstborn with regard to inheritance if he is his father’s first son, and the second son is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest for five sela coins.
messages.quote: The first son is a firstborn with regard to inheritance

messages.text: “But if she bears a girl” (Leviticus 12:5): the apparently superfluous term “she bears” serves to include a child born by caesarean section.

verse.he: וְאִם־נְקֵבָה תֵלֵד וְטָמְאָה שְׁבֻעַיִם כְּנִדָּתָהּ וְשִׁשִּׁים יוֹם וְשֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֵּשֵׁב עַל־דְּמֵי טׇהֳרָהֿ׃
verse.en: If she bears a female, she shall be impure two weeks as during her menstruation, and she shall remain in a state of blood purification for sixty-six days.

notes.he: במס' נדה פ' יוצא דופן (נדה דף מ.) ואם נקבה תלד לרבות יוצא דופן דהוי לידה מעליא ויושבת עליו ימי טומאה וטהרה הלכך גבי וילדו לו נמי לידה מעליא חשיב ליה דגמרינן מהתם:
notes.en: [Rabbi Shimon] follows his reasoning, for he said: in tractate Nidda, chapter Yotzei Dofen (40a): “And if she bears a female” comes to include one born by caesarean section, that it is a proper birth and she observes days of impurity and purity for it. Therefore for “and they have borne him” too he counts it a proper birth, for we derive [one] from the other.

notes.he: ואם נקבה תלד לרבות יוצא דופן:
notes.en: She bears: “And if she bears a female” comes to include one born by caesarean section.

messages.text: And the same applies with regard to a firstborn for inheritance.

And Rabbi Shimon also rules that the second son is a firstborn with regard to redemption from a priest for five sela coins, as he maintains: A firstborn for only one matter, i.e., one who opened his mother’s womb but is not her first child, is considered a firstborn with regard to the redemption of the firstborn, despite the fact that he is not his mother’s first child.

notes.he: כגון שני דהוי בכור לרחמים הוי בכור לכהן אבל ראשון אע"ג דבכור לדבר אחד הוא דהא הוי בכור לוולדות ולזכרים אפ"ה לא הוי בכור דבפטר רחם תלא רחמנא:
notes.en: A firstborn for one matter: such as the second, who is a firstborn of the womb, is a firstborn for the priest. But the first, although he too is a firstborn for one matter, being first among the children and among the males, is nevertheless not a firstborn [for the priest], since the Merciful One made it depend on the opening of the womb.

notes.he: וא"ת מהאי טעמא גופיה דהיוצא דופן בכור לחמש סלעים ואע"ג דכתיב ביה פטר רחם כדאשכחן בסוף פ' שני (לעיל בכורות יט.) דתנן יוצא דופן והבא אחריו ר' טרפון אומר שניהם ירעו עד שיסתאבו ומפרש בגמ' דמספקא ליה בכור לדבר אחד אי הוי בכור אי לאו ואע"ג דהתם נמי כתיב פטר רחם י"ל דסברת ר"ש חלוקה מר' טרפון ואע"ג דהבא אחריו פשיט ליה טפי דהוי בכור מר' טרפון מ"מ יוצא דופן גרע ליה וממעט ליה מפטר רחם:
notes.en: A firstborn for one matter is a firstborn: And if you say: for this very reason let the caesarean be a firstborn for the five sela, even though “opening the womb” is written there. For we find at the end of the second chapter (above, Bekhorot 19a) that we learned: [an animal] born by caesarean and the one after it: Rabbi Tarfon says both should graze until they become blemished; and the Gemara explains that he is uncertain whether a firstborn for one matter is a firstborn or not, even though “opening the womb” is written there too. One may answer that Rabbi Shimon’s reasoning differs from Rabbi Tarfon’s. Although it is clearer to Rabbi Shimon than to Rabbi Tarfon that the one after it is a firstborn, nevertheless he holds the caesarean to be lesser and excludes it through “opening the womb.”
